rows.Notes: The Crowded Corner - With Darrin Davis set to return in the next few cycles there roster construction starts to get a bit strained. Davis who has now missed significant time in back to back seasons cant be relied upon to continue to play LF. Davis obvious place is at DH. That would push Ernesto Quintero out of the (DH) spot. Quintero , last years #1 MLB prospect, has completely broken out , at age 24, has has himself currently in ROY and MVP conversations. Quintero , who plays 3B/1B, would most certainly be kept in the lineup. That starts the strain. Franchise heavyweights currently hold those positions, however, both are FA after this season. Martin Richards (3B) and Mark Aitken (1B) are both multiple times gold glove winners and champions with As. Martin, currently 30 years old, overall rating sits at 88. Mark Aitken (1B), is currently 33 and overall rating sits at 94. Both numbers are down from their previous season but still rank as high level contributors. Buford Park (3B) who has spent most of the season as a back up platoon role is likely going to need to see everyday at bats , whether with As or eslewhere, to maximize his own potential. Kevin Clark (3B), who is currently tearing apart the minors, looks to be ready for a roster expansion call up but hard to see him not on the everyday roster next season. Very interesting decisions to be made here and some of them may be coming sooner than we want.

rows.Notes: The farewell season reaches its final regular season curtain call as the As play host to the NL's top team in the Rockies. As Vinnie Keane HOF career comes to its close a legacy that reshaped Oakland stands to honor it. Manager Deacon Seymour in his rookie campaign appeared to call all the right shots as the As rewrote the history books with the most single wins in a season finishing 127-35. Seymour had a few more flawless decisions ready for the final game. Benji Dillon would return to the starting rotation one last time as an A starter , Vinnie Keane would start at 2nd base in his final regular season game. What would unfold next could not have been imagined. Benji Dillon would give up 2 hits, strike out 8 in a W. Vinnie Keane would go 4-5 and in his very last at bat hit a towering 3 run home run into the left field bleachers. Fellow pillar Mark Aitken would hit 2 homeruns, while his FA is still inpending, Isley Kelley would fall short of hitting a homerun and ends the season sitting at 499 career homeruns, Darrin Davis after another injury shortened season follow up his previous season MVP campaign with a solid year, Danny Horn , Eric Taveras Ernesto Quintero all chipped in with a homerun of their own. rows.Notes: Now that the season has come to close we like to take a look back at the players traded this past season and how their seasons played out and who won the trade. Starting with the most controversial is Martin Richards whom was traded at the deadline for a (SS) prospect who days later broke his foot which ended his season. Richards on the other hand , finished with his 2nd best season of his carrer. At age 30 , Richards still has good years remaining for the Mets. Mets won the trade as of now. The second most controversial was trading playoff hero Peter Busch. Busch was shipped to Cleveland with young arm Jose Baez for a top 20 2B prospect Liam Wade. Also, you can see this as A's choosing Vladamir Gonzalez over Busch. In that framing the trade looks a little better on paper but lets not sugar coat this, Peter Busch is a star. Finishing in top 10 in MVP voting shouldnt sit well with A's fans and the thought of Danny Horn and Peter Busch in the same lineup is tough to get over.  Vladamir is not to be overlooked, however, as he put his best stats of his career up, so the choice had nuiance. Jose Baez struggles mightly and was removed from the starting rotation. Cy Newell and Agustin Rodriguez going to Washington for Travis Coles doesnt need much analysis, Travis Coles is the best pitcher in the MLB. Washington didnt draw a dud however as Cy Newell proved to be a top of the rotation starter, and Agustin Rodriguez started slow but finished strong and is a legit everyday SS with allstar potential. Thomas Gasper didnt show too well so far with the Sox, Buford Park proved to be a consisten everyday 3B for the Yankees and shows a ton of potential, Leo Lamar struggled with the Yankees and Bryan Franco never logged a MLB inning with the Yankees after flashy power in his brief time with the A's. Ultimately A's fared very well in winning the most games in MLB history, Losing Richards and Busch is tough but the moves were of necessity rather than misguided.

rows.Notes: Game 5 of the WS; A's visit the Phillies for game 5. The Oakland A's win the World Series behing John Ellis continued string of strong pitching only giving up 3 earned runs. The bullpen stayed hot in the World Series shutting the door on the Phillies offense. The A's offense continues to be carried by playoff MVP Eric Taveras with his 7th Homerun in this playoff and run. Veterans Mark Aitken and Darrin Davis also add their home-runs. Vinne Keane would get the start and play third base in his final MLB game and would provide a hit and one RBI. Benji Dillon and Vinnie Keane joked after in the locker room celebration that the 7th time is the charm. Mike Paulson celebrated his veteran stars on their season and warned the league of Eric Taveras and Ernesto Quintero taking the bext chapter. Danny Horn , who has stuggled mightly up until the World Series shared that he was glad his bat woke up for the World Series, "after the season I had it would have hung on me if I didnt effect the playoffs". Horn who has zero homeruns leading up to the World Series hit 2 in the World Series and added 8 stolen bases. Deacon Seymour joked that having a record breaking season in his first year sets some unreal expectations going forward.

rows.Notes: The Oakland A's won their 7th championship in the Paulson era lead by stars like Vinnie Keane, Benji Dillon, Mark Aitken, Isley Kelley, Darrin Davis. In a farewell season that will see 2 retire Vinnie Keane and Benji Dillon, 1 potentially leave in free agency Mark Aitken, and 2 remaining to further carry the franchise to the next era Isely Kelley and Darrin Davis. In a seaon where the A's absolutely dominated breaking the single season win records and then only losing 3 games in its playoff run, the A's don't appear as a team on the decline, However with a franchise that AAA team also won its championship, the A's are eager to see the young prospects emerge. But for now the fans of the A's can just rejoice in the perfection the season played out to be. Eric Taveras win World Series MVP to go along with his post-season MVP for the earlier rounds, Taveras showing tremendous value in signing him this past off-season. Pablo Alamanzar continued to show tremendous potential with a no hitter in his MLB debut and then a 1-hitter in his playoff debut and following that up with a game 3 win in the World Series. Arturo Ramos stayed consistent throughout the playoff as well. Championship parade is set for Downtown in c111.

rows.Notes: The Oakland A's celebrated their 7th World Series championship in the Paulson era with a parade and rally in Downtown. Despite the colder temps the Oakland citizens were out in masses to honor their beloved A's. Mike Paulson , Vinnie Keane, Benji Dillon all stood a front the double decker bus cheering and waving to their fans. Darrin Davis, Isley Kelley, and Mark Aitken all laughing and celebrating together to what may likely have a much different feel with Keane and Dillon retiring and Aitken pending free agency unknown. Manager Deacon Seymour and rookie phenon Ernesto Quintero were seen throwing A's beads into the crowd. Playoff MVP Eric Taveras and A's ace Arturo Ramos taking selfie snapshots with fans and dancing with the crowds. The parade ran through Downtown and Jake London Square. After a season of near perfection, the city of Oakland celebrates together, the choices for the direction for next season remain unclear in a few areas but what can be expected is yet another run and the pursuit if championship number 8.

rows.Notes: While the city celebrates its 7th championship in this current era, we take a quick inventory of the choices Mike Paulson is facing this offseason. As there will undoubtably be moves and decisions by Paulson we will not be able to forsee, there are some we can at least speculate on. The biggest decision being the future of franchise icon Mark Aitken. Aitken who is 33 years old would figure to be on the wron side of his peak years but in 2041 posted some of his best offensive numbers of his career. However similar to Martin Richards being traded away to allow the everyday bats for Ernesto Quintero the same script may be the one to read for Kevin Clark. Clark who flashed some potential this past season figures to get everyday at bats which would naturally move Quintero to his second position, first base. Its possible that the emergence of Ernesto Quintero will ultimately seal the fate of Richards and Aitken. Carmen Mesa had looked to be the front runner to take Benji Dillon place in the rotation next season until Pablo Almanzar cemented himself in that slot. Does Mesa return to AAA or will Mesa be moved? Desmond Morton and Frank Reyna are completing for the 1 everyday spot in the OF that is available. The other would be the forth outfielder. This is a story to watch that shapes itself alot like last years decision between Vladimir Gonzales and Peter Busch. Both players figure to have a great career, but you cant keep everyone. Lastly, the bullpen showed some cracks late in the season and the mix of veterans and young arms may need a refresh. As many of the bullpen spots are likely accounted for is their a high end free agent signing that can makes sense.
rows.StoryAngle: The city celebrates its championship, we look at the looming decisions heading into the offseason

Taveras posted on Moltbook that if he was to win anything he would be donating it to the Vinnie Keane Firehouse 29 in West Oakland Baseball Academy. When Taveras was asked how he was able to score so well he shared that its a matter of timing at this point. He went on to say that the instructions were repurposed to be more clear on the objectives and benefited. It should be noted not other contestant that recieved those new "repurposed" instructions scored this well. Former A's third basemen, Martin Richards, had his run on Undocked back in cycle 108 ans scored zero points. rows.Notes: Mark Aitken fresh off one of his best statistical seasons, albiet at the ripe age of 33. Aitken's MLB rating sits at 93 and will be a top ten free agent in this years class. Coming off a record setting season and a World Championship, what is Mark Aitkens Future in the green and gold? Mike Paulson has to make a decision on whether next year starts to infuse the youth movement thats been stacking. Ernesto Quintero emergence force the hand on Martin Richards to make room at third base, there is yet another third base prospect looking for everyday at bat this season in Kevin Clark. In order to make room at third base for Kevin Clark , Ernesto Quintero would have to move to his second position, first base. Mark Aitken has been you anchor at first base this era. So the decision essentially becomes the youth potential in Kevin Clark or the veteran anchor in Aitken. Kevin Clark is an A rated prospect and is MLB rating sits at 79 at just 22 years old. Whether a 22 year old should be your everyday thirdbase man might be the better question

rows.Notes: The Oaks open their inaugural season at home vs the Charlotte Hornets in front of a sold-out crowd and instantly get their first win in franchise history, After 0-9 through rookie camp and preseason the team had grown anxious, and for three quarters it looked like more of the same. The Oaks trailed 36-32 at the half and 60-49 after three. Then they won the fourth quarter 36-22 to win 85-82. Adash Stanley led the way with 27 points on 10 of 15, 4 of 8 from three, with 8 assists, 2 steals and no turnovers in 23 minutes. Austin Reaves added 20 points and 9 rebounds on 6 of 12, 4 of 9 from three and 4 of 4 at the line, also without a turnover. Dillon Brooks was perfect, 5 of 5 for 13 points. AJ Dybantsa had 12 points and 6 rebounds in his NBA debut. Coach Shepard was asked after the game how the locker room responded to the win and he laughed and said his ears were still ringing. Coach Shepard, who is also celebrating his first win as a rookie head coach, emphasized that it was important to honor the moment for its context but to not get too caught up and the next loss could be a game away. Saying that its important to build on the things that were good and eliminate the bad.

rows.Notes: Elias Varek met the media to congratulate his Oaks on their first win and sharing his excitement for what the season has in store. Elias complimented Mike Paulson and Elliot Abraham ability to put togther a quality team in just one off season with hopes that the Oaks will be competitve in their inaugural season. Varek also shared that indeed Jermai Grant failed his medical examination post trade and the matter is with the league. Grant was apart of the trade that sent Draymond Green to Portland after the expansion draft. Just to add more to a volitale situation. The drama if Green returned to the Oaks. Green is currently out with a sprained ankle that was sustained post trade in practice. An intertesting story to track. Lastly, Varek shared that the Oaks stadium would be ready for the first game post allstar game and that the naming rights were purchased by Atlas Bay Architechs, and that the stadium would called Atlas Bay Stadium.

rows.Notes: After getting their first win in their franchise history the Oaks followed with their second win in the very next game. The Oaks traveled to Detroit where its defense would shine in a 91-78 victory. The Oaks trailed 25-19 after one and 43-37 at the half, then won the second half 54-35, holding Detroit to 13 points in the third. Adash Stanley shined with 29 points on 11 of 21, 5 of 11 from three, while Austin Reaves facilitated the action with 10 assists and no turnovers while also contributing 12 points and 7 rebounds. AJ Dybantsa continued his strong start with 14 points and 9 rebounds and little spoken on second round pick, rookie Harry Hayward emerged with 12 points on 6 of 10 and 2 blocks in 12 minutes. T. Jerome added 10 points and 5 assists.

rows.Notes: Watch out now but the Oaks have won three straight games to start the inaugural season. This time the Oaks traveled to New York to face the Knicks and had another convincing win beating the Knicks 115-93. The game was decided in the second quarter, which the Oaks won 48-16 to lead 70-37 at the half. Austin Reaves and AJ Dybantsa lead scoring with 23 points a piece, Reaves on 8 of 13 with 5 of 9 from three, 9 rebounds and 3 steals, while Adash Stanley flirted with his first triple double with 16 points, 11 rebounds and 9 assists. T. Jerome added 17 off the bench on 6 of 10. Harry Hayward repeats his strong performance recording a double double, 11 points and 10 rebounds with 6 on the offensive glass.

rows.Notes: The Oaks now have won their first 4 games to start their first season in the NBA. This latest being the most jarring yet. The Oaks traveled to Washington and blew out the Wizards with a score of 105-62. A 43 point win in just their fourth game speaks to the roster configuration and the coaching in the young season. Washington led 29-26 after one, then scored 11, 9 and 13 the rest of the way, 33 points in the last three quarters. Adash Stanley and Austin Reaves both scored 23, Stanley with 8 assists on 9 of 17 and Reaves on 10 of 18, in a game that mainly featured well orchestrated defense by the Oaks. Dillon Brooks added 12 points and 7 rebounds, T. Jerome 11 on 5 of 8, and T. Henderson Jr. 8 points with 3 blocks. Jonas Valanciunas grabbed 14 rebounds.

rows.Notes: The A's paid Ian Devine and Louis Cross a combined $22 million this past season, and when October came Devine was left off the playoff roster and rookie Clark Saryan took his spot. Cross finished at 0.9 WAR. Hitoki Ka was the best arm in the pen with a 0.90 ERA and Mariano Rosales saved 42, but the cracks showed in World Series game 2 when Saryan and Rosales gave up 2 runs each. With Saryan and Julio Valencia pushing up from the farm, does Paulson move a veteran contract to make room for the kids, or spend the money coming off the books on a high end arm?

rows.Notes: Pablo Almanzar took the rotation spot most expected Carmen Mesa to fill, then threw a no-hitter in his debut and a 1-hitter to close the ALCS. That leaves the rotation full with Coles, Ramos, Rivas, Ellis and Almanzar. Mesa sits at AAA on a $780K deal with nowhere to start in Oakland. rows.Notes: Vinnie Keane made it official this cycle: he is retiring from baseball. The announcement closes a career that went from undrafted to undeniable, with 7 World Series titles in Oakland, an MVP, 7 All-Star selections, 3 Gold Gloves, 5 Silver Sluggers and 436 career homeruns. Keane said goodbye in pieces all season. He hit a 3-run homer in his final visit to New York, went 4-5 with a 3-run homer in his last regular season at bat to close the record 127-35 season, went 3-4 in a playoff game in Minnesota, and started at third base in the World Series clincher in Philadelphia, driving in a run. The parade in C111 and the Blue Lattern Bar night in C112 felt like the end, but this is the formal announcement. Keane is not leaving Oakland. He and his wife Amara live in Grand Lake, where the family opened Keane Mercantile, and the Keane Foundation runs the Firehouse 29 West Oakland Baseball Academy and the annual Keane for Kids Gala. His contract ran through 2041, so nothing is left on the books, only a DH/third base spot and a clubhouse voice to replace as Taveras and Quintero take over. The announcement also turns more light on Benji Dillon, his partner in the farewell season, who still has not said what he will do. Open questions: does Keane take a role with the A's under his friend Mike Paulson, does the franchise retire his number, and does his name go on something at the new Baylight stadium?

rows.Notes: The Darrin Davis Community Youth Events program announced its first event this cycle: the Badge & Paddle Pickleball Classic, a free doubles tournament in East Oakland that puts Oakland kids, neighborhood residents and OPD officers on the same court. Partners are drawn at random, so nobody plays with who they came with. A teenager from Deep East might get a beat officer, a grandmother from Fruitvale might get the Chief. Davis announced it alongside Chief Rafael Montez, and the pairing is the point. The two met three years ago through the A's community policing work, with ride-alongs, youth clinics and school visits in West Oakland and Fruitvale, and what started as PR became a real friendship. Davis majored in criminal justice at Ohio State, was made an honorary police captain in his hometown of Columbus in 2032, and keeps that badge in his locker next to his batting gloves. His line has always been "Baseball's what I do. Justice is what I believe." Davis framed the tournament as the opposite of a crisis response: a chance for people to meet officers on a Saturday when nothing is wrong, and for officers to meet the neighborhoods they patrol by first name. Responders from the Oakland Alternative Response Initiative have been invited to enter a team, putting OPD and the behavioral health crews on the same bracket. OPD is the program's sponsor with support from the A's and Oaks, and every event stays free. Open questions: does Montez actually play, which A's and Oaks players sign up, and does Davis keep the program going if his playing days are winding down at 32 after missing major time twice in three seasons?

Jose Colon has the job and the tools: 27, 84 overall, A potential, a switch hitter with a 72 arm and the Arm Strength Specialist tag. But 2041 was his weakest full season, .250 with a .290 OBP, 16 homeruns, 42 RBI and 1.7 WAR in 97 games, down from .276 with 19 homeruns in 2039. He makes $3.5M in 2042, then goes to arbitration through 2045. The backup outhit him. Henry Calzado, acquired from Baltimore for Julian Porcelli in the 2040 offseason, hit .285 with a .492 slugging, 11 homeruns and 2.4 WAR in 73 games, more WAR than Colon in 24 fewer games, and fielded .997. Calzado is 30, 75 overall with C potential, arbitration eligible 2042 to 2044, and has used all 3 minor league options, so he can't be sent down without waivers. Behind them in Las Vegas are two catchers pushing up. Sergio Aybar, 23, is the A potential prospect at 77 overall and the best defensive catcher in the organization (92 durability, 90 blocking, 86 arm, 80 fielding). His bat jumped this cycle, +6 contact and +6 power against righties, and he can also play third. Marco Fabregas, 24, is the 2038 first rounder, a B potential lefty pull hitter at 72 overall who improved in nearly every attribute this cycle. Paulson has options: ride Colon and bet on a 2039 bounce back, give Calzado more starts, push Aybar to the majors, or shop free agency with as much as $35.9M coming off the books if Dillon and Aitken both go along with Keane. And with two young catchers at AAA, is one of them the trade chip that fixes the bullpen or opens the Carmen Mesa logjam?

rows.Notes: Mike Paulson answered the question this page asked in C114. Carmen Mesa was the A's best trade chip, and now he is gone, sent to the Phillies, the team the A's beat in five games for their seventh World Series title. Mesa, 23, 81 overall with B potential, goes to Philadelphia with relief prospect Porter Broadway, 20, 70 overall with C potential, and second baseman Jose Fuentes, 23, 63 overall with B potential. Coming back to Oakland are third baseman Giancarlo Hernandez and left fielder Antone Baez. Mesa never got a fair shot at a rotation spot here. He was called up in C91 when Henry Rivas dislocated his shoulder, threw a complete game shutout against the Cubs in his first start, 9 innings, 5 hits and 12 strikeouts, and struck out 10 more against the Rays his next time out. When Rivas came back, Mesa was optioned to AAA, and Pablo Almanzar got the late-season call-up and then the fifth rotation spot behind Coles, Ramos, Rivas and Ellis. Mesa, born in Cuba and living in Lake Merritt, was stuck at $780K with nowhere to start. Hernandez is the prize. He is 23, a 2036 first round pick born in the Dominican Republic, wears #15, bats and throws right, and has almost no major league service time. His glove is already elite: 96 fielding, 80 reaction and a 70 arm. The bat is behind the glove, 65 contact against righties and 68 against lefties with modest power, but he hits to all fields and improved in nearly every attribute this cycle, including +9 contact against lefties. He grades A potential at 78 overall and climbing. That gives the A's three young third basemen with A potential. Ernesto Quintero took the job from Martin Richards, and Kevin Clark, 22, was supposed to be next, with Quintero sliding to first base if Mark Aitken leaves in free agency. Baez, 24, 70 overall with C potential, starts in the minors, organizational outfield depth behind Desmond Morton, Frank Reyna and JR Rosado. "I'm not here to replace anyone," he said. "Just here to help." One trade later, he is the one looking over his shoulder. Giancarlo Hernandez arrived from Philadelphia in the Carmen Mesa deal as a third baseman with an A potential glove, and that puts Clark's everyday job in question before he has really had it. Put the two side by side and they are close to mirror images. Clark, 22, from Connecticut, the A's 2037 first round pick, is the hitter: 76 contact against righties and 72 against lefties, 83 discipline, 87 clutch, 57 power against righties, 72 speed and 79 stealing. He is a pull hitter with the Pinch Hitter quirk, and he gained in nearly every attribute this cycle, +6 contact and +6 power against righties, +5 vision and +5 discipline, now 79 overall and climbing. In his 55 at bats this season he hit .327 with 3 homeruns, 11 RBI, 5 steals and 1.0 WAR. Hernandez, 23, is the glove: 96 fielding, 80 reaction and a 70 arm against Clark's 62, 62 and 55, with less bat at 65 and 68 contact. One is the better hitter, the other may be the best defensive third baseman in the organization the day he arrives. Clark also lists 2B and RF as secondary positions, which Hernandez does not, so there may be room for both, though Eric Taveras owns second base and right field already has Vladimir Gonzalez and Frank Reyna. Clark makes $780K in 2042, is under team control through 2047 and has all 3 minor league options left, so the A's can send him to Las Vegas without risk if Hernandez wins the job. Ernesto Quintero is the third piece: he moves to first base if Mark Aitken, the veteran who reached out to Clark the day he was called up, leaves in free agency. Open questions for Deacon Seymour and Mike Paulson: who starts at third on opening day, does Clark's bat play at second or in right, does the club value the 96 glove over the .327 bat, and does Clark, who stepped in when Richards was traded, now see someone step in for him?

rows.Notes: The rumor this page raised in C112 now has a team attached. Word around the league is that the Anaheim Angels have strong interest in Mark Aitken, the A's first baseman and one of the top free agents on the market at 93 overall. Aitken, 33, is coming off a contract year that looked nothing like a decline: .283 with 153 hits, 33 homeruns, 87 RBI and 3.2 WAR in 540 at bats, plus the 3 homerun night against the Phillies and homeruns in the World Series that clinched the seventh title. He made $21.4M in 2041, and any offer that pulls him south will start near that number. The Angels make sense on paper. Aitken was born in California, and a contender in Anaheim could sell him a short drive and a starting job. But Aitken is an Oakland native, and his whole life is here. He owns his place in Jack London, where he lives with his wife and three kids. He is the A's player rep and community liaison, he runs Aitken Little Leaguers, free baseball for East Oakland kids now going into its sixth year, and he shows up at city council and planning hearings without ever testifying, the way he brought Benji Dillon to the DEIR session. He was a major voice in the Baylight negotiations, and he was the veteran who reached out to Kevin Clark the day Clark got the call. P Slayer once wrote that "Aitken is Oakland in a way that can't be replaced." Aitken has not said where he is leaning, but his own words this season point home. On the parade bus after the World Series he said he was watching Vinnie Keane and Benji Dillon take in their last ride, and that he was taking it in too, "for a different reason. I don't know what's next. None of us do." Later he said, "the number on the calendar means more than the number on my back," and that "the contract will sort itself out; the city has a way of holding on to its own, and I've been its own for a long, long time." The A's side of it matters as much. The Mesa trade brought in Giancarlo Hernandez, which gives the club three young third basemen and an obvious answer at first if Aitken goes: Ernesto Quintero slides across the diamond. That makes it easier for Mike Paulson to let him walk, and harder to explain to a city that just watched Keane retire.

rows.Notes: Vinnie Keane made it official in C115. Benji Dillon has not, and the word now is that he is leaving the door open on purpose. Dillon came into 2041 calling it a farewell season, part of the Dynasty Five send-off alongside Keane and Kelley, and when the parade bus stopped after the seventh title it sounded like a goodbye: "you realize you don't have to do it again. That's when you feel the weight of everything you've carried, and it's finally okay to put it down." He has not put it down yet. The 5-time Cy Young winner, 38, made $13.0M in 2041 and went 9-8 with a 4.61 ERA, 120 strikeouts and 56 walks in 140.2 innings, 2.0 WAR, a long way from the 17-6 Cy Young chase of C34 and the 3 career no-hitters, but the A's still trusted him enough to move him to the bullpen in C104, his first relief appearance, and he handled it. His velocity is the story every reporter wants to write and nobody wants to be right about. Dillon has been asking himself the same thing in private. In C109 he wondered, "What's leaving me versus what I'm choosing to let go, is there even a difference anymore?" and after the Keane farewell he asked where he fits now that Vinnie is done. He has reasons to stay home either way. He lives in Rockridge with Maya Torres-Dillon and their son Rick, and he opened the Dillon Clinic there. For the A's, a Dillon return would be a choice, not a need. The rotation behind Coles, Ramos, Rivas, Ellis and Almanzar is set, and Carmen Mesa is gone to Philadelphia. In C108 Mike Paulson called the A's without Keane and Dillon a sobering thought, and C115 counted the money that comes off the books if Dillon and Mark Aitken leave with Keane.

rows.Notes: Ten cycles ago this page was asking Wilson Shepard for answers. The Oaks went 0-4 in rookie camp and 0-5 in the preseason, 0-9 before they had played a game that counted, and in C109 the media wanted to know why the team was losing and why the full roster had never been on the floor together. Shepard, a first-year head coach who spent the previous season as an offensive assistant in Minnesota, kept saying the same thing. In C107 he said the Oaks would "catch people off guard this year." In C109 he said, "We're still finding our rhythm. The guys are putting in the work, and I'm confident we'll tighten up and be ready for the real deal. We're not getting the results we want, but we're not letting it get us down either." In C110, after the loss to Miami, he said the full team had yet to suit up as one, that opening night would show a team nobody had seen, and that he was not worried. The fans were. Nine games into the real deal, the Oaks are 8-1, have won four straight and are 1-0 in the NBA Cup. They beat Charlotte 85-82 in the franchise's first game, coming back from 11 down after three, won in Detroit, New York and Washington, lost by four in Indiana after coming back from 20 down, then routed Toronto 135-75 and beat Oklahoma City, Orlando and Philadelphia. They are scoring 109.9 a game and allowing 89.6, a margin of more than 20 points a night. The surprise is how they are winning. Shepard came in as the offensive specialist, but the early identity is defense: Charlotte scored 82, Detroit 78, Toronto 75 and Washington 62. He has also found rotation pieces nobody expected, like second-round rookie Harry Hayward, and kept the bench fresh, with nobody playing more than 28 minutes in the Toronto rout. After the opener he laughed that his ears were still ringing, then said the next loss could be a game away and the job was to build on the good and eliminate the bad. The other half of this story is the man above him. Mike Paulson is president of operations for an 8-1 expansion team, with Elliot Abraham running the day-to-day as GM, and he is also the GM of the A's in the middle of an offseason that has already seen Vinnie Keane retire, Carmen Mesa traded to the Phillies, Mark Aitken drawing Angels interest in free agency and Benji Dillon undecided. In C110 fans worried that a first-year coach, a first-time GM and a front office chief busy with a World Series run was too much uncertainty. So far the Oaks have answered that. Then there is Elliot Abraham, the first-time GM who has said almost nothing since C111. That cycle, with the team 0-9, he told the media nobody was panicking, that the losing was intentional and that every variation they tried was data for the long term. He also said the Draymond Green trade "wasn't ideal form" for a player the community reveres, and that Jerami Grant's status was a matter the league was looking into. In C112 Elias Varek confirmed Grant had failed his medical and credited Paulson and Abraham with building a quality team in one offseason. Abraham has not spoken since. His path here is not a typical basketball one: born in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, adopted young by an American family, MIT, the man who built the first successful professional pickleball league, then senior operations under Varek at Civis Systems and Paulson's day-to-day operator in his one season with the Chicago Bulls before Oakland hired him in C101. The Bulls beat his Oaks in the preseason in C110. He lives in Jack London, has been seen staying late in the clubhouse after wins, and around the waterfront he is still more of a familiar face than a public one.

They won their second NBA Cup game 147-114, the most points in franchise history, topping the 135 they put up in Toronto. Oakland led by 5 after one, by 18 at the half and by 23 after three, then scored 42 in the fourth. The shooting numbers barely look real: 63 of 79 from the field, 80 percent, and 19 of 26 from three, 73 percent. AJ Dybantsa went 8 for 8 for 18, Wendell Carter Jr. went 8 for 8 for 17 with 9 rebounds, Adash Stanley went 6 for 6 for 15 with 3 of 3 from deep, Harry Hayward went 5 for 5 and 4 for 4 from three for 14, and J. Valanciunas went 3 for 3 for 6 with 6 rebounds in 10 minutes. That is 30 for 30 between them. The leading scorer came off the bench. T. Jerome scored 28 on 12 of 16 with 10 assists in 28 minutes, his second big night as the sixth man after his 19, 7 and 7 in Toronto. Austin Reaves bounced back from his 4 of 14 night in Philadelphia with 27 points on 11 of 14, a perfect 5 of 5 from three, 12 assists and 2 steals in a team-high 41 minutes. Dillon Brooks added 14. Hayward keeps forcing the issue. In 19 minutes he added 4 assists to his perfect shooting, and he is now 9 of 10 from three over his last six games. G. Trent Jr. hit 2 threes in 3 minutes and J. Champagnie handed out 4 assists. B. Simmons was a DNP for the fifth straight game, and T. Henderson Jr., B. James Jr., J. Tate and Coen Carr also sat. rows.Notes: Ten games into their first season, the Oakland Oaks are the number one team in the NBA.com power rankings, ranked first of all 31 teams, and holding the top spot from the week before. The rankings are built on season record and recent form, and the Oaks had both: 9-1 when they came out, 3-0 over the last week, 6-1 over the last two weeks. They earned it against real opponents. Four of the teams in the top nine are teams the Oaks have already beaten: Detroit, ranked 3rd, beaten 91-78 on the road; Oklahoma City, ranked 4th, beaten 101-95 in the Cup opener at home; New York, ranked 6th, beaten 115-93 on the road; and Philadelphia, ranked 8th, beaten 120-106 on the road after trailing by two going into the fourth. Ranked 2nd was San Antonio. The rankings only update once a week, and these came out a game behind. Since then the Spurs came into Oakland for a Cup game and won 126-117, handing the Oaks their first ever home loss. So number one is now 9-2, number two is 8-2, and the gap at the top is half a game. For an expansion team that went 0-9 through rookie camp and the preseason, with a first-year head coach and a first-time GM, being ranked first in the league at all is the story.

rows.Notes: The free agency question this page has carried since C112 has its answer, and it is not Oakland and it is not Anaheim. Mark Aitken has signed with the Colorado Rockies, one year for $21 million. The Angels were the team with the reported interest in C116, the A's were the team with the history, and Colorado is the team that closed. The money is almost exactly what he made in 2041, $21.4M, so this was never about Aitken being priced as a player in decline. He is coming off a .283 season with 153 hits, 33 homeruns, 87 RBI and 3.2 WAR in 540 at bats, a 93 overall first baseman with 3 Gold Gloves and the 2037 Playoff MVP, and he homered in the World Series that clinched the seventh title. The length is the detail that will be argued over. One year is a short commitment for a player at the top of the market, and it puts Aitken back in free agency after 2042. Whether that reads as a door left open or simply the deal that was there, he has not said. What it leaves behind in Oakland is bigger than a lineup spot. Aitken is an Oakland native who grew up swinging a bat in East Oakland. He owns his place in Jack London, where he lives with his wife and three kids. He has been the A's player rep and community liaison, and he runs Aitken Little Leaguers, free baseball for East Oakland kids heading into its sixth year. He showed up at city council and planning hearings, brought Benji Dillon to the DEIR session, was a major voice in the Baylight negotiations, and was the veteran who reached out to Kevin Clark the day Clark was called up. In C114 he wrote that "the number on the calendar means more than the number on my back," and that "the city has a way of holding on to its own, and I've been its own for a long, long time." This time the city did not hold on. For the A's, the move this page laid out in C116 now happens: Ernesto Quintero slides across the diamond to first base. That opens third base outright to the bat-or-glove contest between Kevin Clark, .327 in 55 at bats with 83 discipline and 87 clutch, and Giancarlo Hernandez, the 96 fielding glove from the Carmen Mesa trade. It also comes in the same off-season Vinnie Keane retired, which means the A's go into 2042 without the two longest-standing local voices in their clubhouse. Mike Paulson's choice is now on the record: Aitken walks, and the club trusts its young infield.

rows.Notes: The same cycle Mark Aitken left for Colorado, the A's locked up a player they intend to keep. Vladimir Gonzalez, the A's right fielder, has agreed to a five-year, $119 million contract, $23.8 million a year, avoiding arbitration. It is the biggest raise on the roster this off-season. Gonzalez made $2.7M in 2041, so the new deal adds $21.1M a year, almost exactly the $21.4M that came off the books when Aitken signed with the Rockies. Mike Paulson let a 33-year-old walk on a one-year deal and put the same money into a 28-year-old for five. He earned it. Gonzalez, born in the Dominican Republic, is a 92 overall right fielder coming off the best line of his career: .306 with 161 hits, 28 homeruns, 76 RBI, 17 steals and 4.7 WAR in 527 at bats, with only 60 strikeouts. That 4.7 WAR is more than Aitken's 3.2 and more than any A's hitter this page has written up this off-season. The deal also settles a question Gonzalez raised himself. In C113, with the outfield crowded behind him, he said he was not sure how his clutch performance would affect his chances, that "it's up to Paulson to decide," and named Desmond Morton and Frank Reyna as the players pushing him. He told the young guys, "you can't control what Paulson decides. You just control how you show up," and added, "I earned my spot, sure, but I remember what it was like trying to crack a crowded room." Five years answers who plays right field. It also means Reyna, Morton, JR Rosado and Kevin Clark, whose secondary positions include right field, are competing for left field and the bench.

rows.Notes: In C73 Danny Horn said he was the best player in baseball. He was coming off a 2040 season of .280 with 32 homeruns, 98 RBI, 35 steals, a .524 slugging, an .879 OPS and 8.0 WAR, and the claim started an argument. In 2041 he made it for himself. The A's center fielder hit .338 with 210 hits, 48 doubles, 9 triples, 56 homeruns, 113 RBI, 152 runs and 80 stolen bases in 148 games, with a .382 on-base, .715 slugging and a 1.097 OPS. He was caught stealing only 9 times, struck out just 65 times in 671 plate appearances, and made one error in 1,279 innings in center field for a .997 fielding percentage. His 13.3 WAR is 5.3 more than the season he made the claim. He led the league in hits, doubles, homeruns, runs, stolen bases, slugging and OPS, and won the MVP, the Hank Aaron Award, the batting title, the home run title, his second Silver Slugger and his fourth All-Star selection. The start of his career looks nothing like it. Horn was a fourth round pick in 2029 who hit .166 in 58 games with Minnesota in 2033 and .192 there in 2034, then .214 and .198 in his first two seasons in Oakland. Since then he has hit .246, .259, .322, .280 and .338, and 28.8 of his 42.4 career WAR came in the last three seasons. His career line now reads .268 with 1,143 hits, 246 homeruns, 643 RBI and 208 steals in 1,122 games. He is 30, rated 99 overall, and signed at $37.8M a year through 2044 before free agency in 2045. Horn is also bringing back his wiffle ball tournament. It started in C79 in West Oakland, sponsored by Horn to celebrate the Stabilization Fund, and moved to Temescal, where Horn lives, in C80. The second annual tournament is in Dimond this year.

rows.Notes: The Oaks are winning games after halftime, and they have done it since the first game in franchise history. In Philadelphia they trailed 82-80 going into the fourth, scored 40 and held the 76ers to 24 for a 120-106 win. In Denver in C116 they were already up 23 after three and still put up 42 in the fourth of a franchise-record 147-114 win. Even the Indiana loss showed it. Down 61-42 at the half and 82-62 after three, the Oaks scored 38 in the fourth, won the quarter 38-22 and came within four, 104-100. Through 13 games the Oaks have won the fourth quarter 10 times, lost it twice and tied it once. One of the two losses was the Orlando game, which was already decided at 101-76 after three. The other was the home loss to San Antonio, tied 90-90 going into the fourth before the Spurs won the quarter by 9. Wilson Shepard's young team finishes. In Indiana a 19-point halftime hole was too much. In Golden State a 15-point hole was not.
